Rules for Processing the Personal Data of Project Participants

 

With a view to ensuring security and respecting and upholding the rights of individuals, with particular regard to the right to privacy, the Campus Bemke Foundation presents this policy to explain the rules governing the use, collection and processing of personal data.

When processing personal data, the Campus Bemke Foundation follows the guidelines below, ensuring fairness and transparency of processing as well as efficient exercise of the rights of data subjects.

1. Principles relating to the processing of personal data:

  • “processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner”
  • “collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes”,
  • “adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes — data minimisation”,
  • “accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date”,
  • “kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed”,
  • “processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of personal data: protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical and organisational measures”.

2. Lawfulness of processing:

  • the data subject has given consent to the processing of their personal data for one or more specific purposes;
  • processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract;
  • processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject;
  • processing is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person;
  • processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller;
  • processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, except where those interests are overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject which require protection of personal data, in particular where the data subject is a child.

What data we collect about you

  • Data collected during recruitment.
  • Data of contractors and contractors’ employees collected during contract negotiations and performance.
  • Data of people using services provided by Campus Bemke.
  • Data of people participating in social projects and public-benefit activities carried out by our Foundation.
  • Contact details enabling us to respond to enquiries and correspondence.
  • Data of donors, stakeholders and people involved in building the Campus Bemke project.
  • Data necessary for volunteering activities.
  • Data of people using Campus premises in order to ensure physical and organisational security.
  • Images of people who have consented to their publication.

If you are under 16 years of age, we will ask your legal guardian for consent.

Data Controller
The controller of your personal data is the Campus Bemke Foundation, with its registered office in Klecza Dolna at ul. Krakowska 4, 34–124 Klecza Górna, entered in the National Court Register of Associations, Other Social and Professional Organisations, Foundations and Public Healthcare Institutions under KRS number 0000960145, NIP 5512653624, REGON 521472833.

Contact point
You can contact us by e-mail at kontakt@bemke.pl or in writing by sending correspondence to the registered office of the Campus Bemke Foundation.

Purpose of data processing
Your personal data obtained in connection with your participation in the projects we offer will be processed for the following purposes:

  • recruitment and cooperation,
  • performance of concluded contracts,
  • direct marketing,
  • responding to enquiries and correspondence,
  • implementation of social projects and public-benefit activities,
  • building relationships with stakeholders, collaborators and people supporting the Campus Bemke Foundation,
  • volunteering activities,
  • fulfilment of statutory objectives,
  • ensuring physical and organisational security,
  • responding to letters and applications,
  • archiving,
  • fulfilling legal obligations incumbent on us,
  • managing social media.

Legal basis for data processing

  • the data subject has given consent to the processing of their personal data for one or more specific purposes;
  • processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract;
  • processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject;
  • processing is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person;
  • processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller;
  • processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, except where those interests are overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject which require protection of personal data, in particular where the data subject is a child.

Automated decision-making
Your personal data will not be processed by automated means, including profiling.

Retention period for your personal data
The period for which your personal data is processed depends on the purpose of the processing. The period for which your personal data will be stored is calculated based on the following criteria:

  • legal provisions that may require the Campus Bemke Foundation to process data for a specified period,
  • the period necessary to protect the interests of the data controller,
  • the period necessary to perform contracts and provide services by the Campus Bemke Foundation, and to provide the necessary support to Project Participants and people using Campus premises,
  • limitation periods for claims,
  • the period for which consent has been granted.

Recipients of your data
Your data may be disclosed to:

  • entities providing IT services,
  • Polish Post and courier companies,
  • delivery companies,
  • security companies,
  • entities authorised to receive Personal Data under applicable law,
  • advisory firms, including law firms,
  • Founders of the Campus Bemke Foundation.

Transfer of data outside the European Economic Area
Your personal data will not be transferred to a third country or an international organisation.

Your rights in connection with data processing
You have the right to:

  • access your personal data,
  • have it rectified (corrected or supplemented),
  • restrict its processing or have it erased,
  • data portability in relation to personal data you have provided to us, i.e. the right to receive that personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and the right to transmit that data to another controller; where technically feasible, you have the right to request that we transmit your personal data directly to another controller,
  • the right to object to further processing of your personal data.

You have the right to withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing of your data based on consent before its withdrawal.
If you have any doubts as to whether your personal data is being processed correctly by the Campus Bemke Foundation, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office.

Cookies

General information

1. The website is operated by the Campus Bemke Foundation.
The website collects information about users and their behaviour in the following ways:

  1. Through information voluntarily entered in forms.
  2. Through cookie files stored on end devices (so-called cookies).
  3. Through the collection of web server logs.

2. Information in forms.

  1. The website collects information voluntarily provided by the user.
  2. The website may also record information about connection parameters (timestamp, IP address).
  3. Data provided in forms is not otherwise disclosed to third parties.
  4. Data provided in a form may constitute a database of prospective customers registered by the Website Operator in the register maintained by the Inspector General for Personal Data Protection.
  5. Data provided in a form is processed for the purpose resulting from the function of the specific form, e.g. to handle a service request or business contact.

3. Information about cookies.

  1. The website uses cookies.
  2. Cookies are IT data, in particular text files, stored on the Website User’s end device and intended for use with the Website. Cookies usually contain the name of the website they originate from, the time they are stored on the end device and a unique number.
  3. The entity that places cookies on the Website User’s end device and accesses them is the Website Operator.
  4. Cookies are used for the following purposes:
    • creating statistics that help us understand how Website Users use the website, enabling us to improve its structure and content;
    • maintaining the Website User’s session (after login), so that the User does not have to re-enter their login and password on every subpage of the Website;
    • determining a user profile in order to display tailored materials in advertising networks, in particular the Google network.
  5. The Website uses two main types of cookies: session cookies and persistent cookies. Session cookies are temporary files stored on the User’s end device until they log out, leave the website or close the software (web browser). Persistent cookies are stored on the User’s end device for the period specified in the cookie parameters or until they are deleted by the User.
  6. Web browsing software (web browsers) usually allows cookies to be stored on the User’s end device by default. Website Users may change these settings. The web browser makes it possible to delete cookies. Cookies can also be blocked automatically. Detailed information on this subject can be found in the browser’s help section or documentation.
  7. Restrictions on the use of cookies may affect some functionalities available on the Website.
  8. Cookies placed on the Website User’s end device may also be used by advertisers and partners cooperating with the Website Operator.
  9. We recommend reading the privacy policies of these companies to learn the rules governing the use of cookies for statistics: Google Analytics Privacy Policy.
  10. Cookies may be used by advertising networks, in particular the Google network, to display advertisements tailored to how the user uses the Website. For this purpose, they may retain information about the user’s browsing path or the time spent on a given page.
  11. With regard to information about user preferences collected by the Google advertising network, the user may view and edit information resulting from cookies using the following tool: https://www.google.com/ads/preferences/.

4. Server logs.

  1. Information about certain user behaviour is logged at server level. This data is used solely for website administration and to ensure the most efficient provision of hosting services.
  2. Viewed resources are identified by URL addresses. The following may also be recorded:
    1. time the request was received,
    2. time the response was sent,
    3. client station name — identification performed via the HTTP protocol,
    4. information about errors that occurred during HTTP transactions,
    5. the URL of the page previously visited by the user (referrer link) where access to the Website was made via a link,
    6. information about the user’s browser,
    7. IP address information.
  3. The above data is not associated with specific individuals browsing the website.
  4. The above data is used solely for server administration purposes.

5. Cookie management — how to give and withdraw consent in practice?

  1. If the user does not want to receive cookies, they can change their browser settings. Please note that disabling cookies necessary for authentication, security and maintaining user preferences may make it difficult and, in extreme cases, impossible to use the website.
  2. To manage cookie settings, select your browser or operating system from the list below and follow its instructions:
    1. Internet Explorer
    2. Chrome
    3. Safari
    4. Firefox
    5. Opera
    6. Android
    7. Safari (iOS)
    8. Windows Phone
    9. BlackBerry.

 I. GOOGLE ANALYTICS
To analyse user behaviour, we use Google Analytics, a web analytics service provided by Google Inc. (hereinafter “Google”). Google anonymises the IP address before analysing user behaviour online.

Google has been certified under the Privacy Shield framework, which provides assurance of compliance with European privacy legislation.

Google Analytics uses cookies that are stored on your computer and enable analysis of how you use the website. Cookies used by Google Analytics may be temporary or persistent files, generally with a maximum lifetime of no more than two years. Information generated by cookies about your use of the website is usually transferred to a Google server in the USA and stored there.

Because we have activated IP anonymisation, your IP address is shortened within Member States of the European Union or other states party to the Agreement on the European Economic Area before being transferred to a Google server in the USA. Only in exceptional cases, over which we have no control, is the full IP address transferred to a Google server in the USA and shortened there. On our behalf, Google will use this information to evaluate your use of our website, compile reports on website activity and provide us with other services related to website and Internet usage. The IP address transmitted by your browser as part of Google Analytics is not combined with other Google data.

You can prevent cookies from being stored by selecting the appropriate settings in your browser; however, please note that this may limit the functionality of the website. You can also prevent the data generated by cookies and relating to your use of the website (including your IP address) from being transmitted to and processed by Google by downloading and installing the browser plug-in available at: https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout?hl=pl.

More information about how user data is handled in Google Analytics can be found in Google’s privacy policy at:
https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/6004245?hl=pl.

II. DEMOGRAPHIC DATA IN GOOGLE ANALYTICS
This website uses a Google Analytics feature called “demographic data”. This enables reports to be generated containing information about the age, gender and interests of website users. This data comes from Google’s personalised advertising and user information from third-party providers. The data cannot be attributed to a specific person. You can disable this feature at any time using the ad settings in your Google account or generally block the collection of data by Google Analytics.

III. FACEBOOK PIXEL
We use the Facebook Pixel from Facebook Inc., 1601 S. California Ave, Palo Alto, CA 94304, USA, on our websites to monitor conversions. It allows us to identify website users who were redirected to the site after clicking a banner on Facebook.

The data collected on this website is anonymous to us. We are unable to use it to identify specific users. Facebook may, however, archive and process it in a way that enables it to be linked to the relevant user profile and use it for advertising purposes in accordance with Facebook’s Privacy Policy concerning personal data. This enables Facebook to display advertisements both on its own platform and outside Facebook. As the administrator of this website, we have no control over how this data is used.

For more information about privacy protection, see Facebook’s Privacy Policy concerning personal data at:
https://www.facebook.com/about/privacy/.

IV. GOOGLE MAPS
This website uses Google Maps via an API. The use of Google Maps requires the storage of the IP address. This information is generally transferred to a Google server in the USA and stored there. The operator of this website has no influence over this data transfer process.

Google Maps is used to present our online offering attractively and to make it easier to find the locations listed on the website. This constitutes a legitimate interest within the meaning of Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.

More information about how user data is handled in Google Analytics can be found in Google’s Privacy Policy at:
https://www.google.pl/intl/pl/policies/privacy/.

V. ONLINE APPLICATIONS AND FORMS
Our website offers various ways to contact us. In addition to contact forms, we also use application forms for jobs and cooperation, as well as registration forms and newsletter subscriptions. When using these forms, it is usually necessary to provide us with your personal data. This data is processed only within the scope and for the purpose for which it was provided and with your explicit consent.

VI. NEWSLETTER
If you agree to receive our Newsletter at your e-mail address, you may withdraw your consent at any time by unsubscribing from the subscriber list via the unsubscribe link at the bottom of each newsletter.

VII. OUR FACEBOOK PAGE
The Campus Bemke Foundation and Facebook are joint controllers of the data of users who have liked the Campus page. Accordingly, the Campus Bemke Foundation, as administrator of the page, may obtain anonymous statistical data about visitors to the page through a function provided by Facebook. This data is collected using cookies, each of which contains a unique user code (active for two years and stored by Facebook on the computer hard drive or other storage medium of people visiting the page). The user code, which can be linked to the login data of users registered with Facebook, is retrieved and processed when the page is opened. Although this data is anonymous, the Campus Bemke Foundation may ask Facebook to process it in relation to:

  • demographic data (including trends relating to age, gender, marital status and employment status),
  • information about lifestyle and interests,
  • geographical data that makes it possible to determine where special promotions or events should be organised and how best to target information offers.

At the same time, the data of people who have liked the Campus Bemke Foundation’s Facebook page may be processed in non-anonymised form in the case of:

  • Communication through Messenger available on Facebook,
  • Commenting on posts shared on the Facebook page,
  • Participation in various promotional campaigns or competitions — in such cases processing will be carried out on the basis of the User’s explicit consent, in accordance with the rules of the relevant campaign.

Under no circumstances will the data of people who have liked the Facebook page be used for any purpose other than that for which it was provided. It will be processed exclusively on Facebook and in accordance with the platform’s general terms of use.

VIII. CHANGES TO THIS POLICY

We undertake to review this Privacy Policy regularly and amend it where necessary or advisable due to: new legislation, new guidelines from authorities responsible for supervising personal data protection processes, and best practices in the area of personal data protection. We also reserve the right to amend this Privacy Policy in the event of changes to the technology used to process personal data (where such changes affect the wording of this document), as well as changes to the methods, purposes or legal bases on which we process personal data.
